sections.html:
Bedford County covers 769 square miles of Piedmont Virginia, reaching toward the Blue Ridge, with the town of Bedford as the county seat. The 2020 census counted 79,462 residents. Much of the newer housing serves people who commute to Lynchburg or Roanoke or who want to live near Smith Mountain Lake.

The town of Bedford was an independent city from 1968 until it rejoined the county as a town on July 1, 2013. An old deed or letter that mentions the city can confuse things, so ask which office has your parcel on its books. Some unincorporated areas also carry a Bedford or Lynchburg mailing address, which means the address on an envelope may not match the locality that taxes the property. Look for the county name on your bill.

Real estate tax comes due twice a year.

PaymentDue dateBill
First halfJune 5Separate spring bill
Second halfDecember 5Separate fall bill

There is a recent billing change. Until 2026, one spring bill carried two payment coupons. Starting in 2026, owners get two separate bills, one in spring and one in fall. Pay the whole year with the spring bill and no fall bill follows.

You can pay four ways:

  • Online by bank draft or credit card.
  • By mail.
  • In the drop box.
  • In person at the county office, 122 East Main Street, Bedford, VA 24523.

Your bill shows the rate and any late charges; if it does not, call 540-586-7601. Ahead of a sale, ask the treasurer which bills have been paid, because you may have covered only the first half.

Bedford is reassessing all real estate, and the new values take effect January 1, 2027. The county hired Wingate Appraisal Service, a firm approved by the Virginia Department of Taxation, to do the work.

Appraisal staff started visiting neighborhoods on March 19, 2025 and were scheduled to keep going for 15 months. They look at the outside of each property, may take photos for internal use only, and leave a flyer when nobody is home. Their vehicles are marked Real Estate Assessment/Wingate Appraisal Service, and staff wear ID badges. If someone shows up without them, call the county.

Virginia law requires localities to bring assessed values up to current market value from time to time, and this is that update. The county said owners would get notices in fall 2026, so watch your mail. Questions go to the Reassessment Office at 540-587-0745.

The local Board of Equalization hears appeals. Ask the Reassessment Office for the filing window that fits your notice, since it depends on when the notice went out.

Virginia Code section 58.1-3381 requires the board to consider and decide every petition. The board has three options on any value: raise, lower or leave it. An owner gets word before any increase. Virginia Cooperative Extension describes the board stage as taking one to three months.

Still unsettled after the board? Circuit court is next, under section 58.1-3984. The filing window is the later of three years after the end of the tax year or one year after the assessment date, among other listed cases. The court starts from the assumption that the assessor is right, so the owner has to bring more convincing evidence.

  1. Open the notice when it arrives and mark the appeal window.
  2. Call the Reassessment Office with questions about how the value was set.
  3. File with the board if you still disagree.
  4. Go to circuit court only if the board outcome is not acceptable.

sections.h2: Sell before or after the new values apply?
sections.html:
That depends on the number on your notice. A higher assessed value means a bigger bill after January 1, 2027, and a lower one means less. If you are deciding whether to sell, compare the notice with what you expect a buyer to pay.

  • Read the notice as soon as it arrives and note the appeal window.
  • If the value looks wrong, ask the Reassessment Office how a review is requested.
  • Ask the treasurer for a payoff figure for the current year before you close.

Lenders and buyers read the new assessment too, so a high value can complicate a sale even when the house is sound.

sections.h2: Unpaid tax and transfer costs when you sell
sections.html:
Taxes follow the house, not the owner. A lien for unpaid real estate tax sits ahead of other claims under Virginia Code section 58.1-3340, so the closing agent pays it first out of what the buyer sends. Your contract decides how much of this year's bill each side covers.

Virginia caps what a locality may add for lateness at 10 percent of the overdue tax or $10, whichever is more, and 10 percent a year in interest (section 58.1-3916). Bedford's actual terms are a question for the treasurer.

Two deed taxes come up at the table. Section 58.1-802 sets the grantor tax at 50 cents per $500, normally on the seller. Section 58.1-801 sets the recordation tax at 25 cents per $100.

sections.h2: Who to call in Bedford County
sections.html:
Different questions go to different offices, and calling the right one first saves a week.

  • Treasurer, 540-586-7601: which bills are paid, how to pay, and a payoff figure for closing.
  • Reassessment Office, 540-587-0745: how your 2027 value was set, the appeal window and the review process.
  • County office at 122 East Main Street in Bedford: in-person payments and the drop box.

Jot down the date and who you spoke with. If a title company later questions a figure, you can point to the call.

sections.h2: Steps to sell a Bedford County house
sections.html:
One workable order: confirm on the county records that your parcel is in Bedford County and not the town or Lynchburg; gather recent bills and the assessment notice; request a payoff figure from the treasurer; judge whether the new value is fair enough to leave alone or worth a board filing; then pick a route, either an agent listing or a direct offer.

A listing means repairs, showings and waiting for a buyer's loan to clear. A direct cash offer skips those steps, though the closing agent still collects the tax balance from the proceeds. On either path, put the current year's split in the contract and hold on to proof of payment.

Heirs, landlords with a tired rental and owners who now live elsewhere are the usual people who want a quick exit. A coming reassessment, two bills a year and a list of repairs can tip the choice.

Cash Home Buyers makes written offers on Bedford County houses in their present condition. Call or text the address. Nothing needs fixing first, and no lender has to approve a buyer.

faqs.q: When are Bedford County property taxes due?
faqs.a: June 5 and December 5. Starting in 2026, owners receive two separate bills, one in the spring and one in the fall.

faqs.q: When does the Bedford County reassessment take effect?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027. The county said notices would go out in fall 2026.

faqs.q: Who is doing the Bedford County reassessment?
faqs.a: Wingate Appraisal Service, hired by the county and approved by the Virginia Department of Taxation. Call 540-587-0745 with questions.

faqs.q: Is the town of Bedford separate from Bedford County?
faqs.a: It was an independent city from 1968. It went back to town status and rejoined the county on July 1, 2013, and it is the county seat.

faqs.q: How can I pay my Bedford County real estate tax?
faqs.a: Pay online, by mail, in the drop box, or at the county office at 122 East Main Street, Bedford. Online options are bank draft and credit card.
